issue.summary: On the Teamily iOS app the AI Rewrite control sits inside the chat composer, in the icon row directly under the text input field - exactly where the thumb naturally lands while typing. Tapping it by accident, which the reporter says happens very easily, rewrites/overwrites the text the user has already typed, so the draft is destroyed and has to be retyped. The reporter notes that Rewrite is not a high-frequency feature on mobile and suggests confirming with Aiden whether the button can simply be hidden on mobile, and asked for this to be tracked as high priority.
steps: Open the Teamily iOS app and enter any chat conversation.
Tap the message input field and start typing a message (the keyboard opens).
While typing, accidentally tap the AI Rewrite icon in the composer toolbar - the grey sparkle / 'magic' glyph in the icon row below the input field, circled in red in the attached screenshot.
Observe that the text already typed is rewritten / overwritten and the original draft is gone.
issue.expected: Typed input must not be silently destroyed by an accidental tap. Tapping the AI Rewrite control should either require an explicit confirmation before applying, or preserve the original draft so the user can undo / restore it. Per the reporter's suggestion, the mobile app should consider hiding this non-high-frequency control altogether, or moving it out of the direct typing/thumb area.
issue.actual: A single accidental tap on the AI Rewrite control replaces the text the user had already typed - the draft is lost and must be retyped. There is no confirmation step and no undo. Because the control sits in the composer area where the finger is already operating while typing, the reporter states it is 'especially easy' to hit by mistake. The screenshot shows the composer with the Rewrite control circled in red and an empty input field showing only the 'Type a message...' placeholder, while the iOS Pinyin candidate bar is still active - consistent with an in-progress typing session whose text has just been wiped from the field.
